title: Reporting queries on a shop database

steps.label: Revenue per category
steps.note: Multiply inside the aggregate: SUM(qty * price) per category. printf formats the money with two decimals.
steps.sql:
SELECT p.category,
       printf('%.2f', SUM(s.qty * p.price)) AS revenue
FROM sales s
JOIN products p ON p.id = s.product_id
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY SUM(s.qty * p.price) DESC;

steps.label: RANK() OVER
steps.note: A window function ranks rows within each category without collapsing them, which GROUP BY alone can't do.
steps.sql:
SELECT p.name, p.category, SUM(s.qty) AS sold,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.category
                    ORDER BY SUM(s.qty) DESC) AS rank_in_category
FROM sales s
JOIN products p ON p.id = s.product_id
GROUP BY p.id
ORDER BY p.category, rank_in_category;

steps.label: Running total
steps.note: SUM(...) OVER (ORDER BY month) accumulates across the grouped months.
steps.sql:
SELECT month,
       SUM(qty) AS units,
       SUM(SUM(qty)) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS running_total
FROM sales
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;

steps.label: NOT EXISTS
steps.note: Products that never sold. EXISTS stops at the first matching row, so it stays cheap on big tables.
steps.sql:
SELECT name
FROM products p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sales s WHERE s.product_id = p.id)
ORDER BY name;

steps.label: CTE + self-join
steps.note: WITH names a subquery (a CTE) so it can be used twice: January joined to February per product.
steps.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT product_id, month, qty FROM sales
)
SELECT p.name, jan.qty AS jan, feb.qty AS feb, feb.qty - jan.qty AS change
FROM monthly jan
JOIN monthly feb ON feb.product_id = jan.product_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = jan.product_id
WHERE jan.month = '2026-01' AND feb.month = '2026-02'
ORDER BY change DESC;
